findings.violation: The 60-day return window is claimed to match the pilot data pattern, but the artifact never presents or justifies this specific window from the pilot results presented. A reader cannot verify why 60 days was selected.
findings.fix: Either cite the pilot data passage establishing the 60-day window, or remove the claim that it matches the pilot pattern and justify the 60-day choice explicitly as a policy decision.
findings.evidence: The text states: 'This recommendation applies to items returned within 60 days of their due date; items still unreturned past that window remain subject to the existing replacement-cost billing process, matching the return-rate pattern the pilot data actually established.' The pilot data description mentions an 'on-time-or-eventual return rate' (94%) but does not establish a 60-day window.
